A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multilingual misinformation and unlearning study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite restructuring.

before.justification: V2 reports original multilingual contamination and unlearning experiments, human evaluation, sensitivity analyses and multilingual benchmark results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds a ten-example experiment using ROME factual editing.

M1.justification: The proposed retain/forget objective, gradient descent/ascent procedure and 50:50 English/source-language unlearning mixture remain unchanged. ROME is evaluated separately without revising the proposed combined-language procedure.

E1.justification: The news-contamination task, nine principal languages, related-language tests and multilingual GSM/ARC coverage are retained. The ROME experiment uses a subset of the existing German-contamination scenario and previously evaluated query languages. Expanded corpus-provenance documentation does not establish replacement of the evaluated corpus.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated ROME factual editing in Section 4.7 and Appendix J, whereas v2 only cited its underlying work. Table 8 compares English, German and combined edit variants. The existing gradient-based and real-news-only comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V3 specifies GPT-4o where v2 stated GPT-4 for fake-content judging and verification, and adds a neutral score-5 anchor to QR. It also revises source-abstract provenance from collected authentic news to generated abstracts and introduces the ten-example ROME protocol. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The ROME experiment adds a limited check of whether the language-dependent findings extend beyond gradient-based unlearning. The LoRA sensitivity, related-language unlearning, human-judge validation and perplexity analyses already appeared in v2; their relocation or redisplay adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: The checkpoint boxplots and GPT–human discrepancy/error-bar display are retained. Neither version specifies seeds or repeated-run counts, and v3 introduces no new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds ROME results: German-query fake-response counts are 10 initially and 9, 5 and 4 after English, German and combined edits, respectively, out of ten examples. Retained numerical results are unchanged. V2 Table 2 becomes v3 Table 7, while v3 Table 2 redisplays existing perplexity values.

T1.justification: The retain-minus-forget optimization objective is mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: Both retain the same central claims: injected misinformation spreads across languages, English-only unlearning is insufficient, and combining English with the contamination language improves removal across languages. The revised title and misinformation terminology do not redefine these substantive contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds the justification that generated source news is realistic enough to count as real and interprets ROME results as corroborating the findings. It removes the limitation that combined unlearning may inadequately capture complex multilingual interactions. The transfer-versus-memorization explanation is retained in Appendix G.

D1.justification: V2 describes dataset construction at a high level. V3 adds an extensive operational recipe in Appendix A, including prompts for topics, abstracts, false-detail injection, expansion, paraphrasing, filtering and question generation, and explicitly discloses synthetic provenance. It also supplies a code/data repository link; the existing training hyperparameters and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds Choi and Pawelczyk to position prior unlearning as dependent on English-source information, and Zhang and Zhao for multilingual enhancement. It drops the Xinyue Shen jailbreak reference. The main related-work themes remain; many other bibliography changes are publication updates rather than new cited works.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: Background moves before the experiments, the detailed multilingual-behavior discussion moves to Appendix G, and perplexity-based identification gains a main-text subsection. The title, abstract and many paragraphs are edited, terminology is standardized, and Ethical Considerations is replaced by Acknowledgements.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and existing figures and examples receive revised labels and expanded captions. The output-language table moves to the appendix, a shortened perplexity table is displayed in the main text, and Table 8 presents ROME results. Most scientific graphics and the two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Detailed curation prompts, explicit synthetic provenance, a stated code/data link and clearer presentation improve transparency and usability relative to v2. ROME adds limited corroboration on ten examples. The main evidence remains unchanged, and v3 removes a substantive multilingual-interaction caveat, so the net quality gain is modest.
